Consult Summary:
- Female patient with acute left-sided migraine-type headache with aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, and worsening with movement; patient worried about brain tumor; plan includes headache diary, acute analgesics, consideration of prophylaxis, and follow-up next week with urgent return if red flags develop.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute severe headache on the left side started around mid-day (today), with associated nausea and vomiting. Visual aura described as zig-zag lines prior to onset; blurred vision; photophobia requiring sunglasses.
- Timeline: Symptoms began mid-day today and have persisted for several hours. Prior similar headache occurred a few weeks ago, lasting a couple of days.
- Exacerbating factors: Headache worsens with movement and neck movement/strain.
- Relieving factors: Rest and previously used painkillers helped during the prior similar episode.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea, vomiting (twice today); photophobia; aura.
- Review of systems: No fever, no skin rash, no speech difficulty, no limb weakness, no balance problems reported.
- Other history: Patient is concerned about brain tumor after researching symptoms; family history notable for mother with migraines and mother with underactive thyroid; friend’s mother died of brain tumor; no diagnosed migraines in patient prior to this episode.
- Past medical history: Not explicitly documented; patient reports no prior neurological diagnoses.
- Medications: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) for contraception; on it for about 3 months. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social history: Works in the fashion industry; stressed at work; lives alone; does not smoke or drink alcohol; little to no exercise.
- Family history: Mother with migraines; mother with an underactive thyroid; no other brain disease noted.

- Issue 1: Migraine-type headache with aura (unilateral left-sided, throbbing, photophobia, nausea/vomiting; aura preceding symptoms; worsened by movement)
  - Plan:
    - Headache diary to identify triggers.
    - Acute treatment options:
      - Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
      - Co-codamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
      - Ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented.
      - Naproxen — dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Discuss prophylactic therapy if headaches recur; plan to review at next visit.
    - Return precautions: seek urgent care if headache worsens or does not respond to medications; if neck pain worsens; if weakness in arms/legs or vision changes develops.
    - Follow-up: in about one week to reassess; arrange sooner if red flags develop.
  - Rationale: History and features strongly suggest migraine-type headache with aura; repeated episodes within a short period; patient reassured regarding serious etiologies based on history.
